title: How much CO₂ does the vegetation around you absorb? Let's measure it from space.
home: CO₂ Atlas estimates how much carbon plants absorb every month, for any region up to a thousand square kilometres, using free satellite and climate data. The interface comes in English and Portuguese.
regions: Every region you create is saved, with its calculations and monthly history.
search: Start by finding a place. Search any park, town or farm, and its boundary is loaded from OpenStreetMap. Or draw a polygon or a rectangle, or upload a GeoJSON or a shapefile.
form: Name the region, add the population and emissions you want to compare against, then choose the months to calculate. Advanced settings let you tune the model.
progress: Satellite processing runs in the background, with live progress. Sentinel-2 images are cloud-masked, then combined with land cover and NASA climate data. Sped up here; a real run takes a few minutes.
results: And here are the results: the CO₂ absorbed by vegetation, the share of local emissions it offsets, and the productivity per hectare.
atlas: The interactive atlas shows CO₂, net primary productivity, vegetation index, water stress and land cover. Click any pixel to read its values, or switch to satellite view.
breakdown: Totals by land cover and a month by month chart make it easy to compare areas and seasons.
exports: Export a PDF report, a CSV table, or GeoTIFF layers for your own GIS.
m1: CASA turns satellite and climate data into productivity.
m2: Sunlight from NASA POWER, leaf light absorption from Sentinel-2.
m3: Temperature and water stress, plus land-cover efficiency.
thesis: The original thesis results for Oeiras are bundled, and reproduced within one percent.
end: CO₂ Atlas. Open source, built on Sentinel-2, ESA WorldCover and NASA POWER. Find it on GitHub.
